held_question_d_what_the_seat_accounting.question: Does a write on an old site (not a newborn) count as a record being created? (0153 item d; held by 0326 until Q34 is checked). The checker chooses nothing.
implications: A write (Bind) changes no link (rule text l.612-618; T-124), so under the seat's formula Q = eps(d - 1 - qb) it can change charge ONLY by changing a background label qb. The on-file field charge rho never changes at a write under any reading.

Under the seat's recommended reading A (region labels held through every move), no write - on an old site or a newborn - ever changes the PD-34 count (checker: 0 of 696 Binds). So the charge accounting places no constraint on (d), and the criterion proposed with Claude3's 0153(d) recommendation ("yes, when it moves the site off its surroundings' normal count") would never be met under A; it would amount to "no write counts". If (d) is decided, it has to be on other grounds (e.g. PD-20 / PD-37 record-event counting), not on charge.

Under the neighbour-majority readings (B), the written site's OWN count never changes either (its label depends on its neighbours); a write shifts up to four NEIGHBOURS, all one sign, unpaired - on the supplied block every write within two layers on the unwritten side of a one-sided face shifts exactly two (>=3 reading).
Under the own-record reading (C; contradicts PD-34) every write is a lone unit at its own site.

If "a write on an old site creates a record" were taken to relabel that site (or its region) as written surroundings, the PD-34 total would change by minus the relabelled set's A-B imbalance (one A site: -1; one all-A layer of the block: -32), and every relabelled site whose links are not already at two becomes a +-1 charge. So under the seat's accounting, any write-driven relabelling keeps the total only for A-B-balanced sets and keeps charges paired only if done in A-B pairs.
